about: What `seen` is, for cards as a format 2 catalog file holds them, and what `f` is for an `r`. The engine's desk and Studio are both held to this one file. Plain JSON: nothing here needs the engine's code.

rule: seen is SHA-256, written as 64 lower-case hex characters, of the UTF-8 bytes of the canonical JSON of one object, built from the card for one language code L.

The object has up to three members. title is card.title[L], body is card.body[L], note is card.note[L]. A member whose field is absent, not a string, or empty after trimming is left out. Where all three are left out the object is {} and its canonical JSON is the two characters {}.
Trimming is JavaScript's String.prototype.trim on each field: leading and trailing white space goes, a CR inside a text stays.
For card.bodyShape plain (or no bodyShape) the body is the trimmed text as the file holds it, CR and LF kept as written.

For card.bodyShape alts or steps the body is first read as blocks and written back, in this order. Reading: split the text on LF. A line is a marker when its trim matches ^\[(step|alt)(:[^\]]*)?\]$. A marker closes the block before it (if there was a marker before it) and opens a new one; lines before the first marker are dropped; a text with no marker reads as empty. A block's text is its lines joined with LF, then trimmed; an alt marker with a label (the :label part) keeps its own line, trimmed, as the first line of its block, and a bare marker is dropped. Empty blocks are dropped and the rest are joined with a blank line (LF LF). Then trim again, and if it is empty, leave the body out. Writing back: split on a blank line (LF, any white space, LF), trim each piece, drop empty ones; a piece whose first line, trimmed, is a marker stays as it is, any other piece gets [alt] (alts) or [step] (steps) and an LF in front; join the pieces with LF LF.

Canonical JSON is JSON.stringify for a string, and for an object its members in ascending order of key (by UTF-16 code unit), each as the JSON string of the key, a colon, and the canonical value, joined with commas inside braces; no white space anywhere. Non-ASCII characters are written as themselves, not as \u escapes; control characters (CR, LF) are escaped as \r and \n.

A body in alts or steps is the one place where text is not kept as written: a CR line end at the end of a block, or on a blank line between blocks, is gone, while a CR line end inside a block stays. The cases crlf-plain and crlf-alternatives hold both.
